title: Homework 2 - Member A
text:
# create vector with pre measurements using combine function
pre_bp <- c(130, 128, 116, 124, 133, 134, 118, 126, 114, 127, 141, 138, 128, 140, 137, 131, 120, 128, 139, 135)

# create vector with post measurements using combine function
post_bp <- c(114, 98, 113, 99, 107, 116, 113, 111, 119, 117, 101, 119, 130, 122, 106, 106, 124, 102, 117, 113)





# create names for the 20 subjects using a character vector
names(pre_bp) <- paste("Subject", 1:20, sep = "_")
names(post_bp) <- paste("Subject", 1:20, sep = "_")

pre_bp

 Subject_1  Subject_2  Subject_3  Subject_4  Subject_5  Subject_6  Subject_7 
       130        128        116        124        133        134        118 
 Subject_8  Subject_9 Subject_10 Subject_11 Subject_12 Subject_13 Subject_14 
       126        114        127        141        138        128        140 
Subject_15 Subject_16 Subject_17 Subject_18 Subject_19 Subject_20 
       137        131        120        128        139        135 

post_bp

 Subject_1  Subject_2  Subject_3  Subject_4  Subject_5  Subject_6  Subject_7 
       114         98        113         99        107        116        113 
 Subject_8  Subject_9 Subject_10 Subject_11 Subject_12 Subject_13 Subject_14 
       111        119        117        101        119        130        122 
Subject_15 Subject_16 Subject_17 Subject_18 Subject_19 Subject_20 
       106        106        124        102        117        113 






#subtract the post treatment level from pre treatment level for each subject and store as vector
diff_bp <- (pre_bp - post_bp)
diff_bp

 Subject_1  Subject_2  Subject_3  Subject_4  Subject_5  Subject_6  Subject_7 
        16         30          3         25         26         18          5 
 Subject_8  Subject_9 Subject_10 Subject_11 Subject_12 Subject_13 Subject_14 
        15         -5         10         40         19         -2         18 
Subject_15 Subject_16 Subject_17 Subject_18 Subject_19 Subject_20 
        31         25         -4         26         22         22 


This shows that two numeric vectors of equal length can be subtracted directly, and R performs the operation element by element. Of the 20 subjects, all but three showed decreases in blood pressure.




mean(diff_bp)

[1] 17


The average decrease in blood pressure was 17.




# we use a logical operator to determine positive values
which(diff_bp > 0)

 Subject_1  Subject_2  Subject_3  Subject_4  Subject_5  Subject_6  Subject_7 
         1          2          3          4          5          6          7 
 Subject_8 Subject_10 Subject_11 Subject_12 Subject_14 Subject_15 Subject_16 
         8         10         11         12         14         15         16 
Subject_18 Subject_19 Subject_20 
        18         19         20 


The output gives the indices and names associated with positive changes.




#one way of doing this is to create a position vector of positive differences
pos_indice <- which(diff_bp > 0)

# returns the elements of the positions listed in pos_indice
diff_bp[pos_indice]

 Subject_1  Subject_2  Subject_3  Subject_4  Subject_5  Subject_6  Subject_7 
        16         30          3         25         26         18          5 
 Subject_8 Subject_10 Subject_11 Subject_12 Subject_14 Subject_15 Subject_16 
        15         10         40         19         18         31         25 
Subject_18 Subject_19 Subject_20 
        26         22         22 


We use [] in R to subset or select certain elements from an object.




mean(diff_bp[pos_indice])

[1] 20.64706


The average decrease in blood pressure was 20.65.

text:
Task 2: Basic Data Frame Practice

1) Create a data frame with four columns

# create a separate character vector for the subject names
patient <- names(pre_bp)

#create data frame using `data.frame()` function
bp_df <- data.frame(patient, pre_bp, post_bp, diff_bp)
bp_df

              patient pre_bp post_bp diff_bp
Subject_1   Subject_1    130     114      16
Subject_2   Subject_2    128      98      30
Subject_3   Subject_3    116     113       3
Subject_4   Subject_4    124      99      25
Subject_5   Subject_5    133     107      26
Subject_6   Subject_6    134     116      18
Subject_7   Subject_7    118     113       5
Subject_8   Subject_8    126     111      15
Subject_9   Subject_9    114     119      -5
Subject_10 Subject_10    127     117      10
Subject_11 Subject_11    141     101      40
Subject_12 Subject_12    138     119      19
Subject_13 Subject_13    128     130      -2
Subject_14 Subject_14    140     122      18
Subject_15 Subject_15    137     106      31
Subject_16 Subject_16    131     106      25
Subject_17 Subject_17    120     124      -4
Subject_18 Subject_18    128     102      26
Subject_19 Subject_19    139     117      22
Subject_20 Subject_20    135     113      22


The big teaching here is that the subject names, up until this step, were stored as the names attribute of the vectors and not as a separate column. In order to use them as the patient column in the data frame we first extracted them into their own character vector. We also note that vector names can automatically become data frame row names, but that row names are not the same thing as a data frame column.


2) Return data frame rows where diff_bp column is negative

#from the data frame, keep rows where `bp_diff` is negative
bp_df[bp_df$diff_bp < 0, ]

              patient pre_bp post_bp diff_bp
Subject_9   Subject_9    114     119      -5
Subject_13 Subject_13    128     130      -2
Subject_17 Subject_17    120     124      -4


This confirms that of the 20 subjects, three of them saw negative differences between the pre and post treatments.


3) Add a new column using a condition

# identify in data frame where post_bp is less than 120 
bp_df$post_bp < 120 # this creates a logical vector

 [1]  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE
[13] FALSE FALSE  TRUE  TRUE FALSE  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE

#create a new column with the logical vector
bp_df$less_120 <- bp_df$post_bp < 120

The key teaching here is that the comparison bp_df$post_bp < 120produced a logical vector, but it did not need to be stored as a separate vector object in order to assign it directly to the data frame column.

title: Homework 2
text:
Create two vectors of pre- and post-measurements from a medical experiment on blood pressure


# create two vectors of pre-measurements and post-measurements using c() function

pre_bp <- c(130, 128, 116, 124, 133, 134, 118, 126, 114, 127, 141, 138, 128, 140, 137, 131, 120, 128, 139, 135)

post_bp <- c(114, 98, 113, 99, 107, 116, 113, 111, 119, 117, 101, 119, 130, 122, 106, 106, 124, 102, 117, 113)


Assign names to the vector elements using paste() function


# give a name to each vector element using paste() function

names(pre_bp) <- paste("Subject", 1:20, sep = "_")

names(post_bp) <- paste("Subject", 1:20, sep = "_")

pre_bp

       130        128        116        124        133        134        118

Subject_15 Subject_16 Subject_17 Subject_18 Subject_19 Subject_20 
       137        131        120        128        139        135 

post_bp

       114         98        113         99        107        116        113 
 Subject_8  Subject_9 Subject_10 Subject_11 Subject_12 Subject_13 Subject_14 
       111        119        117        101        119        130        122 
Subject_15 Subject_16 Subject_17 Subject_18 Subject_19 Subject_20 
       106        106        124        102        117        113 



Calculate the change in blood pressure for each patient


# calculate change by subtracting post-measurements from pre-measurements
# a positive value is a decrease in blood pressure 
# save calculation as a new object

diff_bp <- pre_bp - post_bp
diff_bp

Calculate the average decrease in blood pressure across all patients


# calculate average decrease in blood pressure

Determine which patients experienced a decrease in blood pressure after treatment.
